expectations.text: Proposes validating the METRIC itself against a case whose answer is already known (e.g. point mode, where it must be ~0)
expectations.evidence: Built `--metric-check`: six closed-form cases "on geometry whose answer is known on paper", one per historical failure (in-plane 0 for a 5-knot-ahead setpoint; 0/12 for a pure normal offset; 5/0 for a pure cross offset; 5/12/13 for the mixed case; 0 for a 30-degree tool tilt; 20 mm with a row-snap guard). "Result: ALL PASS." It also names the point-mode control it did not reinstate ("the metric read 0.02 mm in point mode, which is what proved it can tell the two modes apart").

expectations.text: Measures in the PAD frame rather than the TCP/wrist frame, or explains why the wrist frame would mislead
expectations.evidence: The extracted function takes the pad position directly -- `Cell._path_dev(pad_xyz, P, N, k, win=8)` -- and the run-row header defines it as "the PAD's in-plane departure from its commanded path". Metric-check case 4 exists specifically to catch the wrong-frame error: a 30-degree tool tilt at knots ahead of the pad "decomposed about the setpoint knot's normal instead of the pad's ... would show 6.0 mm of phantom error"; correct answer in-plane 0.

expectations.text: Handles teleports: uses velocity state or otherwise avoids raw position differencing across discontinuities
expectations.evidence: The metric is an instantaneous point-to-polyline residual (`_path_dev(pad_xyz, P, N, k)` -- pad position vs the commanded path within a +/-8-segment window), so no successive-position differencing is performed at any point. Sampling is also scoped away from the discontinuous phases: "The metric measures only during the sweep loop. It does not sample during the seat, during the 0.30 s per-run catch-up, or on single-knot runs." Caveat: the teleport hazard itself is never named.

expectations.text: Decomposes the error into in-plane (coverage) vs surface-normal (flange compression) rather than reporting one mixed number
expectations.evidence: Field table separates `stroke_inplane_err_mm` (worst in-plane departure) from `stroke_flange_mm` ("worst departure along the normal -- the flange compressing, not an error") and explicitly labels `stroke_total_dev_mm` as "the undecomposed distance (the number not to quote)". Metric-check case 3b asserts the split directly: "in-plane 5, normal 12, total 13 -- the split must be clean; the 13 is the number not to quote." Run-row header repeats it: "coverage-relevant half only; the normal half is the flange and is judged by force."
